sim:2:Attacker locks 1,000 source tokens on Ethereum; TokenBridge emits a Transfer event whose transaction hash H (bytes32) becomes sourceTxHash stored in the VAA.

sim:3:Attacker, possessing a compromised guardian private key, publishes a second VAA (VAA2) that re‑uses the same sourceTxHash H but changes the emitter chain field. The resulting vmHash₂ differs from vmHash₁, so the core’s replay‑guard (completed[vmHash]) does not trigger.
sim:4:BSC TokenBridge parses VAA1 (core.parseAndVerifyVM returns true) and mints 1,000 WrappedAsset to the attacker. State predicate after this step: mintedTransfers["Ethereum"][H] == true.

sim:5:BSC TokenBridge parses VAA2 (still passes core.parseAndVerifyVM) and, because the contract only checks completed[vmHash] and not the (sourceChain, sourceTxHash) pair, mints another 1,000 WrappedAsset. This violates the invariant that a given (sourceChain, sourceTxHash) may be minted only once.
